Home » Statistical Information » Discography » Discography - Retail » Retail - Audio » Live/1975–85
  • Original
  • Collaboration
  • Compilation
  • Playlist


Commercially released: November 10, 1986
Label: Columbia
Produced by Jon Landau, Chuck Plotkin and Bruce Springsteen
Recorded live by Toby Scott, Jimmy Iovine , Bruce Jackson at various locations
Mixed by Bob Clearmountain at Right Track Recording, The Hit Factory and The Record Plant
Mastered by Bob Ludwig at Right Track Recording, The Hit Factory and The Record Plant
Design by Sandra Choron
Photography by Aaron Rappaport, Annie Leibovitz, David Gahr, Eric Meola, Frank Stefanko, Jacquelyn Walsh,
 Jim Marchese, Jimmy Wachtel, Joel Bernstein, Neal Preston, Peter Cunningham, Watt M. Casey
FoldUnfold

Overview
Released

Overview

Bruce Springsteen's 1986 triple CD, triple cassette and/or 5 LP live album Live/1975-85, Over 3 and a 1/2 hours, split the collection into three thematic sections (Club shows, Arena shows & Stadium shows), the final part was over an hour & twenty-three minutes.

a: Mistitled as "4th of July, Ashbury Park" on some CD box sets.
b: Song never released by Springsteen before, the version on this release omits Bruce saying "All you bootleggers out there in radioland, roll your tapes" right before the song.
c: The short spoken intro is from July 7, 1978 at the Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, California
d: This version edits out a long interpolation near the end which includes an early version of "Drive All Night"
e: Writers: Steve Cropper, Eddie Floyd, Alvertis Isbell.
f: Mistitled as "Caddillac Ranch" on the CD box set
g: Performed night after the election of Ronald Reagan to the United States presidency.
h: Song never released by Springsteen before, although recorded by others most notably by Patti Smith and, later, 10,000 Maniacs
i: The date (December 28) in the liner notes is incorrect; the performance actually dates from the following night, December 29.
j: This performance previously released as the music video for "My Hometown" single
k: This performance was released in 1984 as the B-side of the "Cover Me" single. The song was written by Tom Waits and originally released on his Heartattack and Vine album.
